# rigid-dynamics.types: AppliedForce2D

This slice: AppliedForce2D, AppliedForce3D, AppliedImpulse2D, AppliedImpulse3D, RadialImpulse3D, UniformGravity2D, UniformGravity3D, PointGravity, DragModel, BuoyancyModel, OrbitalElements.

```plato

//==
// # Forces, impulses, and gravitation
//
// What acts on a rigid body: forces and impulses applied at a point, radial
// blasts, the environmental force models (gravity, drag, buoyancy), and the
// Keplerian elements describing the orbit a point gravity produces. Forces
// are in newtons, impulses in newton-seconds, and positions in meters.

//==
// # Applied forces and impulses

// A force applied to a planar body: the force in newtons and the world-space
// point of application in meters.
type AppliedForce2D
    implements IValue
{
    Force: Vector2D;
    ApplicationPoint: Point2D;
}

// A force applied to a spatial body: the force in newtons and the world-space
// point of application in meters.
type AppliedForce3D
    implements IValue
{
    Force: Vector3D;
    ApplicationPoint: Point3D;
}

// An instantaneous impulse applied to a planar body: the impulse in
// newton-seconds and the world-space point of application in meters.
type AppliedImpulse2D
    implements IValue
{
    Impulse: Vector2D;
    ApplicationPoint: Point2D;
}

// An instantaneous impulse applied to a spatial body: the impulse in
// newton-seconds and the world-space point of application in meters.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impulse_(physics))
type AppliedImpulse3D
    implements IValue
{
    Impulse: Vector3D;
    ApplicationPoint: Point3D;
}

// An outward radial impulse (explosion): bodies within Radius of Center
// receive an impulse of up to Magnitude directed away from Center, falling
// off linearly to zero at Radius.
type RadialImpulse3D
    implements IValue
{
    Center: Point3D;
    Magnitude: Impulse;
    Radius: Length;
}

//==
// # Environmental force models

// Uniform planar gravity: the same acceleration, in meters per second
// squared, applied to every dynamic body regardless of position.
type UniformGravity2D
    implements IValue, IForceModel2D
{
    Acceleration: Vector2D;
}

// Uniform spatial gravity: the same acceleration, in meters per second
// squared, applied to every dynamic body regardless of position. World space is
// Z-up here, so downward gravity is negative on Z — `UniformGravity3D.Earth` in
// `rigid-dynamics.library.plato` is the value to reach for.
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - World space
type UniformGravity3D
    implements IValue, IForceModel3D
{
    Acceleration: Vector3D;
}

// Newtonian point gravity: bodies are attracted toward Center with
// acceleration mu / r^2. GravitationalParameter is mu = G * M in cubic meters
// per second squared.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton%27s_law_of_universal_gravitation)
type PointGravity
    implements IValue, IForceModel3D
{
    Center: Point3D;
    GravitationalParameter: Number;
}

// A drag force opposing velocity: force = -(LinearCoefficient * v +
// QuadraticCoefficient * |v| * v). LinearCoefficient is in newton-seconds per
// meter; QuadraticCoefficient is in newton-seconds-squared per square meter.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_(physics))
type DragModel
    implements IValue, IForceModel3D
{
    LinearCoefficient: Number;
    QuadraticCoefficient: Number;
}

// A buoyancy force model for bodies in a liquid half-space. The fluid fills
// everything below SurfaceHeight measured along UpAxis; FluidVelocity is the
// current in meters per second used for relative drag.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buoyancy)
type BuoyancyModel
    implements IValue
{
    FluidDensity: Density;
    SurfaceHeight: Length;
    UpAxis: Direction3D;
    FluidVelocity: Vector3D;
}

//==
// # Orbits

// The six classical Keplerian orbital elements. Eccentricity is
// dimensionless (0 = circular, less than 1 = elliptic, 1 = parabolic,
// greater than 1 = hyperbolic); the four angles are in radians.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbital_elements)
type OrbitalElements
    implements IValue
{
    SemiMajorAxis: Length;
    Eccentricity: Number;
    Inclination: Angle;
    LongitudeOfAscendingNode: Angle;
    ArgumentOfPeriapsis: Angle;
    TrueAnomaly: Angle;
}
```
